facts.fact: A nine-hole course from 1928 by Alister MacKenzie and Robert Hunter, set among coast redwoods on an elbow of the Russian River, just north of the Bohemian Club's grove.
The club describes the course as nestled among majestic redwoods.
Fire-hollowed bases ('goose pens') and sword ferns on a duff floor are common in coast redwood forest (general knowledge; not a claim about a particular tree at Northwood).
The club's own logo could not be found online; a whole redwood tree silhouette, the obvious mark for a club in the redwoods, is avoided, and so is anything of the Bohemian Club (its owl).

concepts.name: The Foot of the Giant
concepts.rationale: Only the foot of a redwood fits in the badge: the flared, fluted cinnamon trunk runs off the top, so the tree reads as too tall to draw. A golf ball rests in the dark goose-pen hollow at its base, sword ferns either side on the red-brown duff.
concepts.symbolism: The giants overhead are what Northwood is known for; the ball in the hollow is the golf among them.
concepts.interpretation: The goose pen and the ferns are typical of the forest, not a particular tree on the course.
concepts.strengths: One subject, no background, reads at 1x: the white ball in the black hollow, the red trunk. Not a tree silhouette, so unlike a club mark built on one.
concepts.tradeoffs: At 16 px the ferns become two green tufts.
